Overall, Neighbor 1 supports class B behavior.

Neighbor 2 is another positive analog, but it is more mixed internally. The strongest basic pKa comparison is unfavorable for the query because the neighbor has a basic site with strongest basic pKa 9.6051, whereas the query has no basic site, so the delta is not defined; that absence of a basic center is treated as a BBB-unfavorable shift in this match-up because it changes the ionization pattern relative to the neighbor. Fraction of sp3 carbons is lower in the query, 0.619 versus 0.7429 (delta -0.1238), and the comparison treats that as favorable in this scaffold context. Heavy-atom molecular weight is also far lower, 284.229 versus 482.389 (delta -198.16), which is a substantial size reduction and aligns with the general BBB preference for smaller molecules. Finally, minimum absolute partial charge is lower, 0.1274 versus 0.3108 (delta -0.1833), which further supports a less polar electronic profile. Even with the basic-site difference noted above, the size and polarity changes make Neighbor 2 overall supportive of BBB crossing.

Neighbor 6 is the last negative analog and is the most clearly mixed of the three negative comparisons. Because several of the major properties either match or favor the query, Neighbor 6 does not strongly support a BBB-negative outcome.

Across the six neighbors, the positive analogs all support BBB crossing, and even the three negative analogs contain multiple query shifts that move toward the BBB-permeable side: higher lipophilicity, lower TPSA where it changes, lower heteroatom or partial-charge burden, and in the positive matches a very high neutral fraction and reduced donor count.
